Title: [LSJ] Questions about the way to present a judge's decision concerning a deal

Messages.Author: clechasseur...@catnip-software.com
Messages.Body:
Since we're having a bit of a disagreement in our playgroup concerning
the topic of deals and how to judge them, I will try to ask questions
to settle our argument.

In a game, two players, A and B, strike a deal. Another player C, is
not sure that honoring this deal is playing to win for B, so he calls
the judge to validate.

1. The judge looks at the table, B's hand, asks B a few questions in
private, then makes a decision.

Can the judge announce his or her decision to the entire table:
1.a) if player B asks him to?
1.b) if player C asks him to?
1.c) if he feels like it, without anyone asking?

1.d) Can the judge announce the decision to player B only, in private?

2. Same initial setup, but somehow, the judge manages to make a
decision without using any priviledged information like B's hand, etc.

Can the judge announce his or her decision to the entire table:
2.a) if player B asks him to?
2.b) if player C asks him to?
2.c) if he feels like it, without anyone asking?

2.d) Can the judge announce the decision to player B only, in private?

Thanks in advance.

Messages.Author: Gregory Stuart Pettigrew
Messages.Body:
clechasseur...@catnip-software.com wrote:
> Since we're having a bit of a disagreement in our playgroup concerning
> the topic of deals and how to judge them, I will try to ask questions
> to settle our argument.
>
> In a game, two players, A and B, strike a deal. Another player C, is
> not sure that honoring this deal is playing to win for B, so he calls
> the judge to validate.
>
> 1. The judge looks at the table, B's hand, asks B a few questions in
> private, then makes a decision.
>
> Can the judge announce his or her decision to the entire table:
> 1.a) if player B asks him to?
> 1.b) if player C asks him to?
> 1.c) if he feels like it, without anyone asking?

No. If the Judge's decision is reliant upon information the other
players do not know about, he cannot tell them anything relating to it.
If he did (c), I would recommend he be ejected from the play space.
That's no different from the Judge looking at your hand and saying
"Wow, that's a lot of Dominate!"

>
> 1.d) Can the judge announce the decision to player B only, in private?
>

If he is asked for a ruling, he has to tell player B if, to the best of
player B's knowledge, player B was playing to win.

> 2. Same initial setup, but somehow, the judge manages to make a
> decision without using any priviledged information like B's hand, etc.
>
> Can the judge announce his or her decision to the entire table:
> 2.a) if player B asks him to?
> 2.b) if player C asks him to?
> 2.c) if he feels like it, without anyone asking?
>
> 2.d) Can the judge announce the decision to player B only, in private?
>

Again, the Judge should give his ruling in private to each of the
players involved in the deal. Legality of a deal is a matter of play
*style* and not *game state*, the Judge should not be limiting player's
play style by telling people how others should play.

--
- Gregory Stuart Pettigrew

As I judged many tournaments in my life, small and big ones(EC04), I
always tell the players and other judges, that I dont anwser to any
deals regarding "playing to win". The problem is that the other players
cannot know if the player is holding true to his deal. So dealbreaking
must always be considered, regarding judge decisions. But which judge
wants to spoil that the dealmaking player said: "maybe I want to break
the deal later". If the judge than tells to the other player, that the
deal is legal, according to possible dealbreaking, the other dealmaking
party than knows, that something is rotten in denmark.

So if somebody is asking me, if the VP/GW deal on his table is legal, I
just tell them, it is always legal, cause they will never know, if
the player is not breking his deal.

Messages.Author: Peter D Bakija
Messages.Body:
eRol wrote:
> So if somebody is asking me, if the VP/GW deal on his table is legal, I
> just tell them, it is always legal, cause they will never know, if
> the player is not breking his deal.

But according to the rules, this isn't actually true. Some deals are
clearly illegal from the outset (two players sit down at a table and
immediately decide to table split 2/3 before any cards are played--this
is not a legal deal for the guy accepting the 2 end of the deal). I
realize that it is difficult to mandate who is or is not accepting an
illegal deal, but you can't simply say "All deals are legal, as someone
might be lying! Bwahahah!"

-Peter

Messages.Author: Salem
Messages.Body:


But the thing is, it's perfectly legal for them to _say_ let's do a 2/3
table split. Their actual play actions are illegal if they're not
playing to win, but they can say whatever the heck they want. Of course,
the actual deal would be legal anyway for the guy getting 3vps.

But the other players should be aware of whether or not a given deal is
likely to be legal, and thus play accordingly. Which is part of the play
skill, being able to judge the other players' true positions, rather
than just their stated ones.
